label: Allocation Comparison Chart
title: Allocation Comparison Chart
summary: Compare category amounts with a supplied reference.
corePrinciple: Use one shared scale so comparison stays honest.

anatomy.title: Current values and references share one visual scale
anatomy.description: The chart combines a current pillar, optional baseline overlay, legend, marker, and category label. The shared scale lets people compare categories directly.
blocks: Current and Recommended explain the two readings when a baseline exists.
The main bar height encodes each supplied value.
A supplied recommendation overlays the same category from the bottom.
Keep the dashed callout focused on the first reference unless another marker is needed.
Use short distinct names that stay readable below the bars.

configuration.title: Show the reference only when it answers a question
configuration.description: Use the data, reference, marker, shared max, and any nonnegative bar-area height to establish a comparison that people can read.
blocks: A recommended value appears only when the data includes a baseline.
Omit the reference when the page only needs current category amounts.
The default bar area is 154px; choose any nonnegative numeric height when the host needs more or less room. Labels and legend add to the total chart height.

states.title: Let the data decide whether comparison appears
states.description: The chart has no selected or pressed state. Its meaningful visual difference is whether the supplied segments include a baseline and whether the marker is shown.
blocks: Current bars stand on their own when there is no recommendation.
The legend and first marker explain the additional reading.

sizing.title: Keep bars and labels inside the same host
sizing.description: The host supplies width, the chart owns the bar width token, and height sets the bar area. 154px is the default; narrow hosts need short category names and a shared scale.
blocks: Use a consistent max when categories are compared across a summary.
Keep labels short enough to sit below their own bars.

content.title: Name categories and use one shared scale
content.description: Category labels carry meaning below the bar. The legend and values should use the same unit and comparison frame.
blocks: Short, distinct labels help people map each value to the right category.
Keep the recommended legend when a baseline changes the decision.
Percentages, amounts, or another unit should share one max and format.

inContext.title: Place the comparison beside its summary
inContext.description: A Card can provide the portfolio label and explanation while the chart owns the category comparison.
blocks: Use the chart beside a summary that explains what the categories mean.
specimen: Current mix compared with the recommended reference

doDont.title: Make the reference and scale easy to trust
doDont.description: The visual pairs use real chart data and show the consequence of changing the comparison frame.
blocks: A fixed percentage frame makes category heights comparable.
Separate automatic scales make the same visual height represent different amounts.
Current and Recommended tell people what the overlay means.
Without the legend, the second reading becomes ambiguous.
Names such as Small & Mid, Large, and Others stay readable.
Long repeated labels compete with the values and crowd a narrow host.

sources.title: Grounded in the public comparison contract
sources.description: This guide uses the published AllocationComparisonChart API, the inspected Figma master, and canonical Storybook stories.
blocks: Allocation, current-only, markers, and sizing examples

Examples use public AllocationComparisonChart and AllocationSegment exports from jfs-components 0.1.60. Bars and supplied baselines share one max; when max is omitted it is derived from the supplied values. The package source caps each baseline overlay with min(baselineHeight, barHeight), so a recommendation above the current value is visibly clipped at the current pillar; the guide records that runtime behavior and does not teach it as an independently scaled bar. No custom segment colors are used.
